svg.title: Finally the house term is the physical Hessian film sandwiched between its two row films; the orbit term is the sum over four initial-site copies of the regulator film. Sandwiching a trace- ideal factor by operator-bounded factors preserves its nuclear bound, with the product of the two operator allowances. Sum the four copied terms and conjugate to the common frame; the fixed Fourier norms cost at most e4 on each side at the wider intermediate allowance. The reflection correction is the sum of its two cross products with the regulated site row, and the fixed extra block contributes 4| Loc(G, 0)|. Addition and the same two-sided multiplication rule give the full trace toll in (DP10)–(DP12). Thus the cancellation there is backed by the massive symbol (MA1), the alias sum (MA6), the real and complex floors, and the actual local row derivative bounds. It does not require treating an arbitrary large block matrix as uniformly trace class.
